sources.entry: muxbar - Menu bar app for tmux session management — list, attach, kill sessions, live preview, and a closed-lid mode for in-bag work. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/1989v/muxbar) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu bar app for managing tmux sessions, with a Keep Awake toggle and a "closed-lid" mode that keeps the Mac running with the lid shut.
summary.what_it_does: The app lives in the macOS menu bar and lists all tmux sessions, sorted attached-first and then by creation date. From the menu you can attach a session in Terminal.app, iTerm2, Warp, Alacritty or kitty, kill it, or open a live preview of its recent output rendered with SwiftTerm. A Keep Awake toggle runs caffeinate -dimsu as a tracked tmux session and also detects and stops external caffeinate processes. Closed-lid mode uses pmset disablesleep plus caffeinate -is so the CPU keeps running with the lid closed, with a timer of 30 minutes to 8 hours or no limit. It also shows Claude and Codex weekly usage limits and per-session token counts, read from local logs, and offers YAML session templates for launching long-running scripts.
use_cases: manage tmux sessions from the menu bar
keep a Mac awake while a build or CI job runs
keep a laptop running with the lid closed in a bag
launch and detach long-running polling or backup scripts
monitor Claude and Codex weekly usage limits
notable: Closed-lid mode keeps the CPU running with the lid shut, without needing an external display, and routes output to an external monitor if one is connected
Keep Awake detects caffeinate processes started outside muxbar and stops them with one click
Long-running script launcher: YAML templates turn tmux sessions into one-click toggles for polling and batch jobs
Shows Claude and Codex weekly limit left in the menu bar icon and per-session token shares, reading only local logs
Passwordless pmset option uses a narrow sudoers rule that only allows pmset
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later and tmux installed via Homebrew
Closed-lid mode needs an admin password (Touch ID) or a manual sudoers rule, and auto-off without that rule only kills the session and sends a notification
Builds are ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so the first launch needs right-click → Open
Open at Login and notifications only work when running as a bundled .app, not via swift run
